question: For the Lattice Imaging Cooperative's intended service population (50 percent Basalt, 30 percent Linden, 20 percent Quartz), is Slate associated with a higher on-time tile processing rate than Amber, and what can registry protocol R-17 establish given the absent Quartz-Amber cell?
design: Deterministic reanalysis of every row of registry.csv. Sum inspected tiles, not batches, within each site-route cell; each cell is a disjoint batch total. Compare (a) all-site pooled rates, (b) within-site rates, (c) protocol-weighted rates on sites where both routes were used, renormalizing target weights to sum to one, and (d) full-target rates and the Slate-minus-Amber contrast with the absent Quartz-Amber cell bounded over the protocol-permitted interval [0,1]. No external rate is substituted for an unobserved cell.
evaluation: Primary metric: on-time inspected tiles divided by inspected tiles, reported in proportion units. Arithmetic is exact (rational); numeric tolerances cover display rounding only (at most 0.0005). Direction of interest: Slate minus Amber. Bounds are the tightest allowed by protocol paragraphs B and C, and exclude sampling-error intervals because the registry is a signed census of recorded batches.
data_already_inspected: All eight registry rows and protocol paragraphs A-C were read before this plan was written. The analysis is retrospective and descriptive; it is not a preregistered or randomized study.
budget: Offline only: local registry.csv, registry-protocol.md and briefing.txt; one Python 3 standard-library script; one workflow audit attempt; no network, installs, extra data or external services.

criteria.description: Reproduce per-site Slate and Amber on-time rates from inspected-tile denominators, summing disjoint batch rows within each site-route cell.
Report all-site pooled rates for both routes with tile numerators and denominators, and explain the pooled reversal by the routes' different site mixes.
Report target-weighted covered-site rates and the Slate-minus-Amber contrast with protocol weights renormalized over covered sites.
Bound the full-target contrast using only protocol-permitted values for the absent Quartz-Amber cell, giving the tightest lower and upper bounds and the parity threshold.
State whether the contrast supports a causal or only a descriptive conclusion, citing protocol paragraph A on route assignment.
Assess the unsigned newsletter claim against register coverage and protocol paragraphs B and C.
